title: HMRC · Trust record keeping for tax purposes
relevance: HMRC identifies trust deeds and supporting records that trustees may need to retain. This is documentary grounding for a trust file, with no inference about the frequency of conflicts.

title: HMRC · Trust Registration Service manual, beneficiary details
relevance: HMRC distinguishes identified beneficiaries from beneficiaries defined as a class. Registration practice supports the genre, while the operative text and documented named membership would determine any in-scope edge.

title: HMRC · Manage your trust’s details
relevance: The service supports updates and downloads of proof of registration showing recorded roles. An administrative snapshot can serve as a credible Source with its own provenance and date.

title: Trustee Act 1925 · section 36
relevance: The provision grounds surviving or continuing trustees, persons nominated by the instrument and written appointments as documentary concepts. The file must establish its own powers and effects.

title: HMCTS · Apply for probate with MyHMCTS
relevance: The professional workflow asks about original wills and codicils and describes a paper route when originals or specified copies are unavailable. Will validity and probate entitlement are outside the graph.

title: HMCTS · Applying for probate if there is a will
relevance: HMCTS distinguishes wills from updates and discusses custody of originals and retention of earlier documents. It provides a setting for filing and version questions.

title: SRA · Drafting and preparation of wills
relevance: The regulator describes private-client instructions, individual circumstances and risks in drafting. It supports a will-planning retainer, with specific onboarding or file-sharing practices left as assumptions.

title: General Register Office · How to apply for a correction to a birth registration
relevance: The original registration information remains visible alongside a dated marginal correction. This documents a useful coexistence of older and corrected assertions without establishing what is typical in solicitors’ files.

title: ContractNLI · A Dataset for Document-level Natural Language Inference for Contracts
relevance: The study distinguishes entailed, contradicted and absent propositions with supporting spans. It provides a diagnostic design analogy from contracts, with no claim about private-client practice.
